task.description:
WF-03 Step 5 -- CLOSE THE ISSUE RECORD for ISS-0426. Every prior gate has PASSED: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (after 2 reworks), SECURITY-REVIEWER, REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (which independently reproduced a mutant and matched its count exactly), and TEST-RUNNER. Follow WF-03 Step 5's own procedure; this description supplies the run-specific facts you need and the one judgement call you must make.

THE JUDGEMENT CALL -- WHICH TERMINAL STATUS. Read ISSUE_QUEUE.md's 'Issue status vocabulary' and decide between `resolved`, `instrumented`, and `no_defect` BEFORE writing the line. Do not default to `resolved`. The relevant facts:
  - A root cause WAS identified and removed for the class that produced the filed failure: {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, _}} is now unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION from the 14 Group 1 call sites (11 no longer call Task.yield at all; 3 no longer evaluate any `after timeout_ms ->` clause). That is a structural removal, not a mitigation.
  - BUT the 11 Group 2 tests still race a real wall-clock timeout by design -- hard constraint 4 REQUIRED keeping that race, because those tests exist to assert the LUA-10 kill actually fires. Their contention exposure is reduced (isolated subprocess, no async siblings, no parallel partitions) rather than eliminated.
  So: the filed defect's root cause is removed; a related residual sensitivity is deliberately retained as required by the issue's own constraints. Judge whether that is `resolved` (root cause removed) or `instrumented` (verified work shipped, root cause NOT removed, requires a superseded_by: pointer). ORCH's reading is that `resolved` is correct because the retained Group 2 race is not the filed defect and was explicitly out of scope by AC4/hard-constraint-4 -- but YOU make the call against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's actual definitions, and if you choose `instrumented` you must file the successor issue pointer. Whichever you choose, use THAT status's own key pair (resolved -> resolved_in_run:/resolved_at:; instrumented -> resolved_in_run:/resolved_at: plus a required superseded_by:; no_defect -> verdict_in_run:/verdict_at:, never resolved_*).

EVIDENCE TO CITE IN THE RECORD (all real, all verified this run):
  - Fix: two additive @doc false test-only seams on Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor (run_script_sync/3, run_with_heap_limit_sync/4). executor.ex diff vs main: 113 insertions, 0 deletions -- AC4 holds, production wall-clock kill semantics byte-for-byte unchanged, config/config.exs:17 untouched. REQ-155's LUA-10 security control intact.
  - 11 genuinely-racing tests tagged @tag :lua_wallclock_race, excluded in test_helper.exs, isolated in a new additive subprocess in letflow.check.test.ex (37 insertions, 0 deletions -- zero existing lines touched, which mattered because that file is shared with the live concurrent run WF03-ISS0418-20260902).
  - Coverage: 8 new tests (seam equivalence across all 4 outcome shapes; memory limit still binds through the unbounded-wait seam; AST-based tag-partition integrity). Fail-first satisfied by MUTATION per WF-03's rule for new code -- 4 mutants each producing a discriminating failure set (4/45, 4/45, 12/45, 1/56), and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently reproduced mutant 1 in a throwaway worktree, matching both the count and the exact failing-test set.
  - TEST-RUNNER's results: full serial `mix test` -> 'Result: 3057 passed (6 properties, 3051 tests), 21 excluded', 0 failures (AC3). Isolated partition -> 11 passed, 45 excluded. `mix letflow.check.test` -> PASS all 3 phases. AC6 -> TWO TEST_PARALLEL_N=6 scripts/test_parallel.sh runs, both 'combined: 3048 tests, 6 properties, 0 failures (3054/3054 passed)', all 6 partitions clean, no ISS-0219/ISS-0222 infrastructure symptoms.

HONESTY REQUIREMENT ON THE RESOLUTION TEXT -- this record will be read by future runs and must not overclaim. State plainly that the ORIGINAL FLAKE WAS NEVER REPRODUCED ON DEMAND: ISSUE-FIXER could not trigger it even under 24 OS-level CPU burners plus 48 concentrated runs of the affected test, and recorded that as an honest negative. The fix therefore rests on STRUCTURAL verification (the failure branch is unreachable by construction, confirmable by reading the diff) with the two clean parallel runs as CONFIRMATORY evidence -- not on having reproduced the flake and then shown it gone. The gate-approved design's section 4 is the authority for that framing. Do not write anything implying the flake was reproduced and eliminated.

ALSO RECORD: the scope_note already in docs/issues/ISS-0426.yaml explains that the wasm half of the filed scope was deliberately left to the live concurrent run WF03-ISS0418-20260902 (which owns lib/letflow/engine/wasm and the three wasm test files). Confirm that note is still accurate, and make clear in the resolution that this run enumerated-but-did-not-edit the wasm-side wall-clock-sensitive tests. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR also filed a MINOR noting AC6's literal criterion; TEST-RUNNER has now satisfied it with two real runs, so that concern is closed -- say so.

GITHUB CLOSE. github_issue is 830. Step 5's evidence-on-close rule is a HARD requirement: close it with `gh issue close 830 --comment "<...>"` using the comment template for the status you actually chose (WF-03 Step 5 item 2 gives the exact wording per status). A close with no comment and no linked PR is this step NOT DONE. Note the PR is not merged yet at the time you run this -- ORCH handles Step Final -- so the --comment form is the one that applies.

Complete the handoff: PASS, next_action 'Route to Step Final'. Commit and push to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902.

result.summary: Terminal status chosen: `resolved` (not `instrumented`, not `no_defect`), judged against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's 'Issue status vocabulary' definitions rather than defaulted. Reasoning: `instrumented` applies when verified work shipped but the underlying defect's root cause is NOT removed -- that does not describe this outcome. The filed defect's root cause (14 Group 1 call sites -- 11 nil-heap, 3 heap-limited -- racing a wall-clock OBSERVATION window via Task.yield/2 or a receive block's `after timeout_ms ->` clause against ordinary BEAM scheduler contention, which produced the filed {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, 5000}} at executor_test.exs:983 where {:error, {:script_error, _}} was asserted) is now structurally unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION from all 14 call sites -- confirmed by a static source/diff read (the 11 nil-heap seams contain no Task.yield call; the 3 heap-limited seams' receive blocks contain no after clause), not by a repeated-run count. That is exactly `resolved`'s bar ('a root cause was actually removed, and a regression test proves it'), and the design's own section 4 states this structural framing is the deliberate preference here. The 11 Group 2 tests that still race a real wall-clock timeout are NOT the filed defect and were explicitly required to keep racing by hard constraint 4 (they exist to prove the REQ-155 LUA-10 kill actually fires) -- their contention exposure is reduced (isolated subprocess, no async:true siblings, no scripts/test_parallel.sh cross-partition contention) rather than eliminated, which is a deliberately retained, narrower, out-of-scope residual risk, not an unremoved root cause of the filed issue. `no_defect` does not apply either -- a real defect was diagnosed and a real fix shipped through every gate. Wrote docs/issues/ISS-0426.yaml with status: resolved, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0426-20260902, resolved_at: 2026-09-03T06:22:12Z (real clock read), plus a `resolution:` block citing all verified evidence (executor.ex 113/0 diff, AC4 production-semantics-unchanged, the 11-test Group 2 tag/isolation mechanism, the 8 new tests with mutation-based fail-first proof reproduced independently by TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER's full serial/isolated-partition/check.test/AC6 results) and stating PLAINLY that the original flake was NEVER reproduced on demand at any point in this run -- Step 1 could not trigger it under 24 concurrent CPU-burner processes plus 48 concentrated AC7-only runs, all 48 passed, recorded as an honest negative -- so the fix rests on structural verification of the diff, with TEST-RUNNER's two clean TEST_PARALLEL_N=6 scripts/test_parallel.sh runs (both 'combined: 3048 tests, 6 properties, 0 failures (3054/3054 passed)') reported as CONFIRMATORY for Group 1 and load-bearing only for Group 2's residual risk, never as proof the flake was reproduced-then-eliminated. Confirmed the existing scope_note (wasm half left to sibling run WF03-ISS0418-20260902) is still accurate and added one sentence confirming the wasm-side tests were enumerated but never edited by this run. Noted TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step-04b MINOR (AC6's literal >=2-repeated-run criterion was out of that gate's own scope) is now closed by TEST-RUNNER's two real runs. GitHub issue 830 closed via `gh issue close 830 --comment "..."` using the `resolved` comment template (cites the run-id, the structural root-cause-removal claim, the honest never-reproduced-on-demand statement, the retained Group 2 race, docs/issues/ISS-0426.yaml, and the regression test path) -- verified via `gh issue view 830 --json state,closedAt`: state CLOSED, closedAt 2026-09-03T06:23:04Z. No lib/ or test/ file touched by this step; only docs/issues/ISS-0426.yaml (owned_modules) and this handoff were written.
